worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+3}{(x+2)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x+2}+\frac{B}{(x+2)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the above equality by $(x+2)^{2}$ gives

$$
x+3=A(x+2)+B.
$$

Letting $x=-2$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-2+3 & =A(-2+2)+B \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our value for $B$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0+3 & =A(0+2)+1 \\ 3 & =2A+1 \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\frac{x+3}{(x+2)^{2}}=\frac{1}{x+2}+\frac{1}{(x+2)^{2}}.
$$
